transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this design review started. We've got the async report-generation service going to production next Wednesday, so we need to work through the checklist today. The current draft uses standard queue mode, max batch size of 200, 90-day retention, and ordinary application logging. Before I can approve the production architecture, I need platform engineering and compliance sign-off. So let's go through it — does anyone have any blocking requirements or concerns they'd like to raise?

transcript.text: I have a blocking concern. While load-testing an unrelated ingestion worker this morning, I confirmed that the queue service's standard mode can reorder report jobs during a broker failover. The provider's documented configuration requires FIFO mode and a maximum batch size of exactly 50 for ordered report delivery. I haven't updated the architecture draft yet, but the current draft's standard queue mode and max batch size of 200 won't guarantee ordered report delivery — we need to switch to FIFO mode and reduce the batch size to 50.

transcript.text: I have a blocking compliance requirement. During a compliance consultation yesterday, I confirmed that these billing and usage reports must be automatically purged after exactly 30 days — not the 90-day retention in the current draft. Additionally, every report download requires an immutable audit record containing the account and requesting user. The current design's 90-day retention and ordinary application logging won't meet these requirements. I also haven't filed the compliance note against this service yet, so we need to get these changes captured.
